proposed_from.topic: Sharp identification of individual-weighted strict Pareto benefit under multivariate response-pattern selection in cluster-randomized trials via a positive-stratum joint completion-and-cross-world LP, with compatibility onset, attained dual-certified bounds, nonrectangularity and majority-threshold results.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest missing-outcome comparators are Wang, Li, and Wang for smooth average effects in cluster trials and Scharfstein, Manski, and Anthony for bounds on scalar ordinal follow-up laws and arm-distribution dominance. The closest direct fraction-benefiting comparator is Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum, whose randomized-trial target is scalar ordinal or binary. Gao, Ge, and Qian provide the clearest fixed-marginal multi-marginal optimal-transport comparator: their Section 1.2, equation (2), and Section 2.2, equation (3), range over couplings with identified marginals, as do the relevant components in Ji, Lei, and Spector and Ober-Reynolds. Fan, Park, Pass, and Shi provide the closest incomplete-data conditional-optimal-transport comparator: Section 2, Assumption 2.1(ii)--(iii), takes \((Y_1,X)\) and \((Y_0,X)\) source laws as identified, and Theorem 3.1 characterizes the corresponding moment-model set. Their model is non-nested with the present one because overlapping component-response patterns do not identify either complete vector arm law; instead they impose intersecting projection restrictions that must be retained while the arm laws and cross-world coupling are jointly chosen. The novelty claim is solely the sharp nonrectangular observed-data set produced by joint missing-state completion and cross-world Pareto transport, together with its observational embeddings and joint dual certificates. The sensitivity-feasibility onset is the domain boundary of that same set, and the finite rectangular construction is an internal strictness diagnostic. Li, Miao, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen instead point identify a full-data law under self-censoring and completeness. No strict improvement over any comparator theorem, no absence of generic incomplete-data conditional optimal transport, and no published rectangular-imputation workflow are claimed.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Derive sharp attained strict Pareto-benefit bounds and constructive min-cut certificates from finite product-ordered arm marginals.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; Propositions 1--2; constructive proof of Proposition 1; Concluding Remarks
seed_details.anchor_read: The chain proof first derives cumulative inequalities and then constructs triangular joint tables. The first changed step is replacing nested thresholds by a nonnested relation neighborhood and completing residual masses outside that relation.
seed_details.summary: Obtain the exact capacities \(D_{R^c}\) and \(1-D_R\), endpoint couplings, explanatory cuts, and polynomial-time algorithms.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the scalar triangular-block construction by a relation-specific maximum-flow decomposition and prove residual row and column supports form a complete rectangle in the complement.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining strict Pareto benefit, finite posets, causal optimal transport, cluster randomization, and min-cut located general transport duality and between-patient CRT wins but no matching package.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Strassen1965 because relation-constrained couplings already satisfy Hall inequalities.
seed_details.rebuttal: The classical existence theorem does not state the two causal endpoint capacities, residual completion algorithm, strict-product-order cut reductions, or individual-weighted CRT information contract as a theorem package.
seed_details.burned_reason: The fixed-marginal Pareto-capacity angle was subsumed by existing transport results; the missing-state pivot yielded sound sharp identification but no inference or empirical package and remained incremental.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Characterize exactly when all compatible couplings assign the same strict Pareto-benefit mass.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; Sections 2--4 on the scalar identified interval and confidence construction; Discussion
seed_details.anchor_read: The scalar paper treats exceptional collapse through an ordinal optimization. The first changed step is to perturb mass around arbitrary positive support rectangles rather than adjacent chain cells.
seed_details.summary: Prove point identification if and only if every support-rectangle contrast vanishes, equivalently the restricted binary relation matrix has identical rows or columns.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace one-dimensional support separation by four-cycle perturbations in the relative interior of the transportation polytope.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for point identification of relation mass, transportation-polytope objective constancy, and Pareto support rectangles found linear-algebraic transport facts but no causal product-order characterization.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the statement that a linear objective is constant on a transportation polytope exactly when its cost is additively separable.
seed_details.rebuttal: Specializing that criterion to positive causal supports, proving the binary identical-row-or-column equivalence, and deriving clinical majority frontiers yields a nontrivial exact characterization absent from the scalar papers.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Construct simultaneous whole-identified-set inference for clustered Pareto capacities at exact and locally switching cut ties.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; equations (1)--(2); Theorems 3.1--3.2; local analysis in Section 3.4; Conclusion
seed_details.anchor_read: The paper proves that full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for standard-bootstrap validity under Gaussian limits and replaces the failed bootstrap by an estimated directional derivative. The finite min-cut derivative is a maximum or minimum over active affine scores.
seed_details.summary: Combine cluster-AIPW marginal influence vectors with joint cut-score calibration to cover both endpoints uniformly without selecting one active cut.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace independent-unit resampling of a generic directional derivative by a cluster multiplier process indexed jointly by lower and upper Pareto cuts, with nuisance learning trained outside validation clusters.
seed_details.destination_search: FangSantos2019 covers generic directional maps, JiLeiSpector2023 covers independent-unit transport duals, and ChenLi2026 covers smooth clustered generalized effects; the exact paired target--method combination was not located.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from FangSantos2019 by plugging the min-cut directional derivative into its bootstrap theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform whole-set coverage requires a joint cluster influence expansion, primitive learner conditions, simultaneous lower and upper calibration, and local cut-switch control not furnished by the abstract theorem.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine when every, some, or no compatible coupling yields strict majority Pareto benefit.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Propositions 1--2; Corollary 1 on stochastic dominance; discussion following Proposition 2
seed_details.anchor_read: The scalar corollary links an endpoint to stochastic dominance. For a product relation, the first changed step is replacing cumulative dominance inequalities by relation-specific Hall deficiencies on upper and lower sets.
seed_details.summary: Give exact cut conditions for guaranteed, possible, and impossible majority benefit, with threshold \(1/2\) replaced by a general clinical threshold when prespecified.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Translate threshold claims into attained endpoint inequalities and then into finite relation cuts.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Pareto majority benefit, fraction benefiting threshold, and multivariate stochastic dominance found scalar benefit and independent-person win probabilities but no same-person cut frontier.
seed_details.red_team: This is only the endpoint theorem evaluated at \(1/2\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection limits this to a corollary rather than a standalone kernel; it is retained only as a decision-facing component of the top-ranked package.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Characterize contraction from pooled to baseline-stratified and full-cluster Pareto information under informative sizes.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; Theorem 1; Sections 2.2--2.4 on covariate-assisted dual bounds; Theorem 2; Discussion
seed_details.anchor_read: The anchor averages conditional sharp transport bounds over pretreatment covariates. The first changed step is preserving the individual-size weighting and then comparing it with transport over labeled within-cluster outcome vectors.
seed_details.summary: Prove sharp nesting, common-active-cut equality for pooled versus stratified bounds, and strict finite witnesses for full-cluster refinement.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace unit-level conditional coupling by roster-conditional cluster-vector coupling with additive same-position Pareto cost.
seed_details.destination_search: JiLeiSpector2023 covers iid covariate refinement and WangParkSmallLi2024 covers CRT weighting, but no theorem comparing these three coupling information contracts was located.
seed_details.red_team: Conditioning always sharpens bounds by Jensen's inequality, so the result is routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: Jensen gives only inclusion; exact equality requires common active cuts, full-cluster sharpness requires coupling vector laws, and strictness under informative size needs separate compatible-law witnesses.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Compose vector-valued restricted missing-at-random recovery with cross-world Pareto transport.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; Theorems 1--3; Proposition 5 sensitivity model; Discussion
seed_details.anchor_read: The paper constructs scaled doubly robust scores for smooth mean effects under incomplete CRT records. The first changed step is estimating or bounding the full joint state indicator, because componentwise response models do not recover the multivariate state law.
seed_details.summary: Derive observed-data arm-state regions under vector restricted missing at random, propagate them sharply through Pareto capacity, and define a critical missingness-sensitivity radius for majority benefit.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace scalar outcome regression in the doubly robust score by response-pattern-specific joint-state recovery and retain outer uncertainty through the transport optimization.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor treats mean effects, while HuangFangHanleyRosenblum2019 assumes the needed ordinal margins are available; no multivariate missing-state Pareto capacity result was located.
seed_details.red_team: Apply the published missing-data estimator separately to each state indicator and plug the result into the capacity formula.
seed_details.rebuttal: Separate componentwise indicators do not identify joint multivariate state probabilities under nonmonotone missingness, and plug-in optimization is nonregular at tied cuts.
seed_details.burned_reason: The fixed-marginal Pareto-capacity angle was subsumed by existing transport results; the missing-state pivot yielded sound sharp identification but no inference or empirical package and remained incremental.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Obtain assignment-based confidence sets for a partially identified same-person benefit interval with few clusters.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; Sections 2--3 on inversion of nonzero randomization nulls; simulation results; Discussion
seed_details.anchor_read: The paper inverts computationally efficient cluster-randomization tests for point-valued effects. The first changed step is formulating a null over a coupling polytope whose optimizing cut can change after one reassignment.
seed_details.summary: Invert the known assignment law for both Pareto endpoints while treating potential cluster outcomes as fixed and the compatible coupling as a composite nuisance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the shifted point-null statistic by a supremum over feasible joint-potential-outcome tables and establish validity after cut reoptimization.
seed_details.destination_search: Randomization-based CRT intervals and scalar fraction-benefiting sampling intervals were found separately, but no exact assignment inversion for a clustered coupling interval was located.
seed_details.red_team: Project any randomization confidence region for arm marginals through the Lipschitz capacity map.
seed_details.rebuttal: That projection is valid but typically conservative and does not solve exact composite-null inversion or exploit the optimizing relation geometry; a sharp finite-sample method remains nontrivial.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Choose a cluster assignment law that minimizes worst-case uncertainty for estimated Pareto-capacity endpoints under informative sizes.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction; Theorem 2 efficient influence functions; Theorem 4 cross-fitted efficiency; Conclusion on covariate-adaptive cluster randomization
seed_details.anchor_read: The paper derives efficiency for a fixed simple randomization and leaves covariate-adaptive designs open. The first changed step is to make the allocation probabilities decision variables in the covariance of all active Pareto cut scores.
seed_details.summary: Derive a minimax allocation over feasible size-adaptive cluster designs with a saddle-point certificate for worst-case active-cut variance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a fixed-design efficient influence variance by a max-over-cuts design criterion and solve the resulting allocation saddle problem.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for optimal CRT allocation, informative cluster size, transport endpoints, and active cuts found Neyman allocation and smooth GCE efficiency but no Pareto-capacity design theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Balanced assignment is automatically optimal by symmetry.
seed_details.rebuttal: Informative sizes and asymmetric active-cut score variances break arm symmetry; optimality requires a design certificate and may depend on baseline roster composition.
